In older Spanish literature and 19th-century orations, the phrase “el azul Neptuno” (blue Neptune) or “un manto de azul Neptuno” was a common classical metaphor used by poets and orators to describe the vast blue ocean or sea. In various historical translations of López Jaena’s speeches and essays, his description of the Philippine islands surrounded by the ocean is translated as having the blue sea (or blue Neptune) as her mantle.
